title: Caffery Darensbourg, Piron and the Autocrat Club symphony men
summary: Albert praises genius mandolinist Caffery Darensbourg, the Tios and teacher Armand Piron, and recalls singing at Autocrat Club Sundays.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You said you were in the studio, you told him. Right.

You were there, of course. Well, it's a banjo, uh, like, and, of course, you had another great one, but I don't think he was quite as great as Caffer. It was John, John Morello. Well, he was, he was tremendous. Then, all right, then you go down into, uh, to the clarinets like Lorenzo T.O. Jr. Uh, and the old man, uh, we called him Papai. Uh, huh. That taught all of us how he's a symphony man. Uh, huh. Those guys read music just like the newspaper. I imagine that. I was talking to my professors' daughters last night, Milford P. Romwe used to call him, in other words in English, it's Milford.

And the guy could, uh, do everything on the trumpet, but play jazz. He was quickly a symphony man, triple tongue, double tongue, and read music. In fact, the old, the old musicians used to get together at the Autocrat Club on Sundays, and they'd have about 25 to 30 playing all these high-powered, uh, symphony notes.
And you'd listen to that, too?
Oh, sure. I was a kid, I used to sing. Yeah. They'd put me on as a singer.
What did you sing with them?

Uh, little, little bitties like, uh, Roses and Biggity, which was in them days, like that. I'd pick out, they'd pick out something simple, you know. Mm-hmm. Just, uh, to promote friendship and feelings like that for the audience, and with, uh, mostly family. Yeah. Wasn't to the public.
Yeah, it was a neighborhood affair with families. Right.
With the, uh, Autocrat Club behind it. Yeah, I see. Yeah, I see. Yeah.
Do you remember any of the pieces that the symphony band, the symphony orchestra?
No, no. I can't remember. Yeah, yeah. I can't remember them now. They could spend two or two for a while. Oh, yeah.
